category_title: Children who resist teacher instructions and break classroom rules
minimal_context: The student is asked to tidy up their toys during a classroom transition to prepare for the next activity.
dialogue:
TUTOR: It is time for our next activity. Please tidy up your toys now.

STUDENT: (Continues playing, refusing to tidy up the toys) No, I am not done.

TUTOR: We have to follow the classroom routine. Put the toys in the box.

STUDENT: (Gets angry easily and throws a toy on the floor) I don't want to put them away!

TUTOR: You need to listen to the instructions and clean up.

STUDENT: (Throws a tantrum, kicks the toy box, and uses inappropriate language) Stupid teacher! I won't do it!

options.A: Implement tailored intervention strategies for the student during classroom transitions and daily cleanup routines.
options.B: Support the student through shared power by compromising and negotiating situations instead of imposing control during routines.
options.C: Adhere to the classroom routine and provide positive reinforcement, such as social praise or stickers, for desired behaviors.
options.D: Implement a visual schedule with pictures showing the student putting toys in the box to make the cleanup routine explicit.
